sampling_model.design: Independent and identically distributed sampling from the observed law \(P\)
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(Y_i,D_i,Z_i)\) on a fixed finite positive-mass cell grid; the finite-sample projection theorem uses the binary-treatment submodel
sampling_model.treatment: The structural calculations allow finite-valued \(D_i\) and impose support and correlation restrictions on target arms \(d\) and \(e\) in \(\mathcal Q^r(P)\). The distinct class \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\) imposes them on every \(a\in\mathcal A\); the two classes coincide on the binary-treatment submodel used for inference.
sampling_model.overlap: The maintained target overlap is \(0<P(D=a)<1\) for \(a\in\{d,e\}\). Equality with the published all-arm identified sets additionally requires \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\ne\varnothing\), which supplies admissible untargeted-arm kernels rather than silently imposing extra target overlap.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cell masses and bounded outcome masses are empirical averages; conditional means are derived only inside the positive-mass primitive map

body.tldr: For finite imperfect-instrument cells, SDC and SDC-plus-LEI reduce target-arm identification to bounded completion polytopes, and exact aggregate support retains exactly the positive-slack branches. Unrestricted cone duals give sharp arm closures and conditional product coupling gives the sharp ATE closure; if the all-arm Ban--Kédagni class is nonempty, its exact target-arm and ATE identified sets coincide with those of the target-arm class. The rational center yields \([711/1100,911/1100]\), strictly inside the normalized outer union, and positive LP margins make this strict inclusion persist on an open two-parameter beta neighborhood of \((79/100,17/20)\). A legal three-cell SDC family has minimum positive slack \(3\varepsilon/2\), a fixed Hausdorff jump, and exact known-pair minimax risk \(3/20\) for every \(\varepsilon_n=o(n^{-1/2})\). Binary-treatment Hoeffding projection covers the whole exact set in finite samples.

project_justification.gap: Ban and Kédagni impose aggregate support equality for every treatment arm but report normalized valid outer bounds and leave sharpness unresolved. Their formulas neither filter algebraically feasible branches by exact support nor establish that target-arm calculations extend to the published all-arm class; an isolated numerical strictness witness would also leave robustness unclear.
project_justification.niche: Finite-cell correlation-cone geometry separates branch feasibility, positive-slack support eligibility, endpoint optimization, and cross-arm coupling. This separation yields an all-arm extension theorem under a nonempty published-class premise, an open neighborhood of strict improvement around an exact rational center, and an explicit SDC branch boundary whose statistical indistinguishability is governed by \(n\varepsilon^2\).
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the positive-slack eligibility equivalence, unrestricted-cone sharp endpoints, exact target-arm and all-arm coupling logic, rational and locally robust strictness certificates, exact SDC discontinuity formulas, an exact \(3/20\) root-\(n\) two-point minimax frontier, and a conservative finite-sample whole-set confidence region.

body.related_work: Ban and Kédagni (2022) supply the all-arm aggregate-support and SDC or SDC-plus-LEI restrictions and valid normalized outer formulas. This paper's target-arm class equals their class on binary treatment; with multiple treatment levels, the exact target-arm and ATE identified sets agree under the explicit premise that the all-arm class is nonempty. The unrestricted cone result strictly tightens their normalized SDC union at the rational center \(P^\star\). With the four cell masses and uniform control cells fixed, the treated laws \(\operatorname{Beta}(100\varrho,100(1-\varrho))\) and \(\operatorname{Beta}(20s,20(1-s))\), centered at \((\varrho,s)=(79/100,17/20)\), retain strict inclusion on an open neighborhood by positive slack, score-feasibility, endpoint-gap, and multiplier margins. Kédagni, Li, and Mourifié (2018) study sharp finite zero-covariance restrictions, a different moment class. Nevo and Rosen (2012) motivate same-direction and less-endogenous correlations. Park (2025) proves joint attainment for a different MIV-plus-MTR problem and is not a tightening target. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), Cho and Russell (2024), Fang and Santos (2019), Bai et al. (2026), Goff and Mbakop (2026), Levis et al. (2025), and Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013) inform generic projection, mathematical-program, nonsmooth, and intersection-bound inference; none supplies the exact support-filtered root-\(n\) nonshrinking lower result proved here. The broader adaptive procedure and its conditioned positive-margin rate remain open. Ban--Kédagni's NLSYM application and Zhanhan Yu's PM2.5 application are same-population-restriction consumers: under the maintained restrictions, the reported population object changes from a valid normalized outer region to the exact support-filtered set with a branch-slack boundary diagnostic.
body.interpretation: The causal objects are the identified sets of \(\theta_a(Q)\) and \(\Delta_{d,e}(Q)\) over compatible full-data laws. The LP unions are observed-law functionals proved to equal the closures of those sets. Positive slack is an exact aggregate-support eligibility condition, not a numerical tolerance. Conditional product coupling proves that armwise endpoint approximations coexist on one full-data law and, when the published all-arm class is nonempty, that untargeted-arm restrictions do not change the target identified sets.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Exact decisions at \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)=0\) require rational arithmetic, interval certificates, or explicit primal--dual tolerances. The local strictness neighborhood relies on finite-LP positive margins and does not assert global robustness. The exact \(3/20\) frontier concerns the known two-point SDC experiment and rules out shrinking along \(\kappa_n=o(n^{-1/2})\); it does not determine an adaptive rate from slack alone. The coverage construction is conservative and binary-treatment, and may require global optimization over positive-mass primitive pairs. Fixed grids, known support endpoints, and independent sampling are maintained; LEI boundary behavior, covariate adjustment, clustered sampling, estimated supports, empirical sign reversal, and unrestricted contraction remain outside scope.
body.honest_scope: The identification kernel is the exact support filter, sharp unrestricted-cone endpoints, and joint target-arm completion. For multivalued treatment, equivalence with Ban--Kédagni's all-arm class is claimed only when that class is nonempty; it is automatic on the binary submodel. The rational four-cell center and its open beta neighborhood, and the three-cell boundary family, are population results rather than empirical findings. The discontinuity and minimax theorem is SDC-only. Finite-sample projection covers the binary-treatment exact set, while a fully adaptive procedure and rate beyond the certified \(o(n^{-1/2})\) nonshrinking frontier remain open.
